chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from some of his companions, that he ascribed it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who does not recognize for anyone a virtue (by having granted him a favor), is one who admires his own belief.

key_terms.الْفَضْل: Virtue, merit, or favor granted to someone
key_terms.الْمُعَجَّبُ: One who is self-admiring or overly impressed by oneself

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'mu'ajjab bi-ra'yih' in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In Maani al-Akhbar, Shaykh al-Saduq links the failure to acknowledge others' merits directly to the spiritual disease of self-admiration (al-mu'ajjab bi-ra'yih), a key concept in Shia ethical theology. This deficiency in recognizing external virtue serves as a diagnostic marker for an inflated ego that invalidates deeds, echoing the Imam's teaching that true humility requires seeing the good in creation as a reflection of Divine grace.
